To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the measurement errors in accruals estimation using balance sheet accounts can lead researchers to erroneously conclude the existence of earnings management, can lead them to erroneously find that accruals are priced in the cross section, and can lead them to incorrectly conclude that accruals predict future stock returns.
the errors in measuring accruals using a balance sheet accrual approach are likely to bias tests for earnings management and market mispricing of earnings and accruals.

(1) the measurement error in balance sheet accruality estimates can lead researchers to erroneously conclude the presence of earnings manage- ment when it does not exist; (2) the measurement error can lead to erroneous conclusions in tests of market mis-pricing of accruals; and (3) the measurement error will confound tests of the association between discretionary accruals and returns.
